S22.28.needs: A workspace folder open in VS Code, and a signed-in account that can run the agent.
S22.28.note: The approve buttons are built from the word "Approve" plus "once" or "for session" in webviewContent.ts (around line 7034), so the full text "Approve once" is not a literal in any file. The exact trigger for the card depends on the agent's mode and the tool asked for; the mode-menu entry point was found only in the QuickPick code (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts), not as a confirmed sidebar control.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel in VS Code and open the mode menu.
Choose "Ask" (the mode that asks before acting).
In the "Describe a task…" box, type a request such as: create a file named notes.txt with one line of text, then press send.
When the approval card appears, read the summary and detail text of what will happen, then compare with Expected: an approve/deny form is shown.
Optionally click "Deny" or "Abort turn" to check the card closes with its outcome message.
S22.28.where: AGI chat panel > "Describe a task…" box: pick "Ask" in the mode menu, then send a task that changes a file. When the agent asks, an approval card appears in the chat with "Approve once", "Approve for session", "Deny" and "Abort turn" buttons.

S22.30.needs: A signed-in account that can get an answer from the agent.
S22.30.note: The table renderer is apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/render.ts (lines 72-74, aria-label "Table" is not visible text). I did not confirm that the sidebar answer view uses this renderer, since webviewContent.ts does not import it, so the table's visible appearance is unverified. The model decides whether it writes a table, so the tester must ask for one.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel in VS Code.
In the "Describe a task…" box, type: compare three database options in a table with columns for cost, speed and setup, then press send.
When the answer arrives, look for a grid with a header row and aligned cells.
Make the table wider than the panel if you can, and check that it scrolls sideways inside its own box rather than moving the whole panel.
Compare with Expected: the comparison appears as a readable table, not as raw pipe characters.
S22.30.where: AGI chat panel > "Describe a task…" box: ask for a comparison, for example "compare two options as a table". A Markdown table in the answer renders as a scrollable table with a region label "Table".
